lesson_title: The Tongue Map Is a Lie
hook_text: Remember the tongue map, with sweet at the tip and bitter at the back? It is wrong.
clip_script: Every part of your tongue with taste buds can taste every taste. The four you learn at school: sweet like honey, salty like biltong, sour like lemon, bitter like strong coffee. Plus a fifth, umami, the savoury taste of gravy. Here is the chemistry clue hiding in your mouth. Sour usually means acid: citric acid in lemons, acetic acid in vinegar, lactic acid in amasi. Bitter and soapy usually means a base, like soap. But now the most important rule in this whole topic. Never, ever taste something to find out what it is. Drain cleaner, bleach and paraffin can look like water and burn you from the inside. Keep them in labelled bottles, never in cooldrink bottles, and lock them away. Scientists use colour-changing indicators instead.
visual_style: Whiteboard tongue map with a big red cross through it; four food icons sorting into taste labels; a cooldrink bottle full of paraffin with a warning symbol and a locked cupboard.
pacing: Quick myth bust, brisk taste tour, slower firm safety message.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn the safe way to test for acids.
